tests.title: exchangeToken mints a real, working access token against a live NetSuite sandbox
tests.description: Drive the pure core end-to-end against a real NetSuite sandbox: build + sign a PS256 client-assertion JWT with a real cert-mapped private key, exchange it at the live token endpoint via a real fetch-backed TokenSender, and assert the response is a 2xx returning a non-empty access_token plus a numeric expires_in (~3600). This proves the assertion claims, kid/certId mapping, scope, and aud host are all accepted by NetSuite — the parts unit tests can only assert against the documented contract, not the live service.

inputs_required.name: ns_account_id
inputs_required.description: A NetSuite sandbox account id. Sandbox ids contain an `_SBn` suffix that the plugin lowercases and hyphenates into the token host.

inputs_required.name: ns_client_id
inputs_required.description: The OAuth 2.0 Consumer Key / Client ID for an integration record in the sandbox that is enabled for the client-credentials (M2M) flow. Becomes the JWT `iss` and POST `client_id`.

inputs_required.name: ns_cert_id
inputs_required.description: The NetSuite certificate mapping id for the uploaded public certificate, used as the JWT header `kid`. Found under Setup > Integration > OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials (M2M) Setup.

inputs_required.name: ns_private_key_pem
inputs_required.description: The PKCS#8 PEM private key whose matching public certificate is registered against ns_cert_id in the sandbox. Provide via env var (e.g. NS_PRIVATE_KEY) or a gitignored fixture file — never commit it. PS256 requires an RSA key.

inputs_required.name: ns_scope
inputs_required.description: The scope string the integration record is authorized for. Defaults to rest_webservices.

tests.implementation_hint: Guard the test with test.skipIf(!process.env.NS_ACCOUNT_ID) so CI without credentials stays green. Read all inputs from env vars; normalizePem the key string. Use the real fetch-based TokenSender (the same shape index.ts wires) rather than the mock. Assert status 200, accessToken is a non-empty string, and expiresIn is a positive number. Do not log the assertion, token, or key. Keep this file out of the default `vitest run` glob or behind an env gate so the offline suite is unaffected.
tests.test_run_summary: Pass: minted a real access_token (non-empty) with positive expires_in against the live sandbox, ~1.4s

tests.title: Minted token authorizes a real NetSuite REST API call
tests.description: After minting a token (ni-0), issue a GET against a known NetSuite SuiteTalk REST endpoint with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and assert a 2xx (i.e. the token is actually accepted by the REST service, not just issued). This closes the loop on the §5 smoke item that a subsequent REST call succeeds.

inputs_required.name: ns_rest_probe_path
inputs_required.description: A low-impact, read-only REST path on the sandbox that the integration's scope can access — e.g. the metadata catalog or a record-type listing. Combined with the account host to form the full URL.

tests.implementation_hint: Reuse the token from ni-0 (chain within the same describe block or mint once in beforeAll). Build the REST base host the same way audUrl derives the token host (accountId.toLowerCase().replace(/_/g,'-') + '.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com'). Assert response.ok / status < 300. Same env-gating and no-secret-logging rules as ni-0. Treat a 401/403 as a credential/scope misconfiguration in the fixture, not a plugin bug.
